text:
jamie: Orchard Health just opened ORCH-1423 — customer reports p95 latency jumped from ~420ms to ~2.1s on their dedicated pool orchard-prod-b4 around 19:12 UTC. Seen across multiple prefixes. Can we triage? :eyes:

megan (support): customer attached a few request_ids: req=0a1b2c, 0a1b2d. They say it started after a traffic spike. They've already retried and saw same. Screenshot + logs in the ticket.

oncall-bot: @eng-runtime oncall is sam (pagerDuty) — escalation routed. Recent deploy: deploy-bot deployed model/redwood-v1.4 to orchard-prod-b4 at 19:07 UTC.

sam: I'm on it. Can someone grab p99/p95 over the last 30m and kvcache hit rates for that pool? Also, did we change batching or quantization for this customer?

dmitri: I see increased IO wait and a few host-level CPU steal events on hosts in orchard-prod-b4 at 19:10-19:25. Looking at the host metrics now. Not seeing kernel updates. Could be noisy neighbor on the host.

lucas: If it's IO/steal it's likely host-level. But we should still collect a flamegraph from the runtime during a spike. If someone can run a quick perf capture on one of the pids, do:

```
sudo perf record -F 99 -p $(pgrep -f redwood-runtime | head -n1) -g -- sleep 30
# then: sudo perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded; flamegraph.pl out.folded > spike.svg
```

sam: grabbing p95/p99 now — posting metrics link in a sec. Also can we capture kvcache stats? Orch pool metrics path: /metrics/pools/orchard-prod-b4.

megan (support): customer confirmed they saw the first error at 19:12 and that traffic dropped a bit after 19:30 when they retried. They need an ETA; saying it's impacting user sessions.

alex: If hosts are noisy we can route traffic to orchard-prod-b3 as fallback and fail open to a lower-latency model variant for the affected customers while we investigate. Suggest a quick routing rule for that pool. :thumbsup:

sam: I don't want rollbacks without data. Can we do two parallel things: 1) collect prof and kvcache metrics, 2) run a synthetic load against orchard-prod-b4 to reproduce. If we can reproduce we can try route/fallback.

dmitri: I can repro a minor CPU steal locally on one node using the same VM class. Will try changing the cgroup cpu.shares for the runtime to see effect. If that stabilizes p95, we know it's contention.

lucas: Also check for a GC pause or jemalloc fragmentation. Add these envs to the runtime temporarily to get extended stats: MALLOC_CONF and set MMTUNE. Example: `MALLOC_CONF="stats_print:true,prof:true"` but be careful on prod.

sam: Collected metrics: p95=2.08s, p99=3.4s at peak. kvcache hit rate dropped from 92% -> 45% during the spike. Looks like KV cache warmed out / eviction storm. That explains throughput collapse.

jamie: Good catch. Anything in the deploy-bot changelog that could trigger different cache keys?

deploy-bot: changelog for model/redwood-v1.4 includes batching tweak: "adaptive-prefix-batching: enabled by default" rolled at 19:07 UTC.

lucas: Adaptive batching could change key prefixing under some workloads and cause cache miss storms. If kvcache hit rate tanked and batching changed request shapes, that fits.

sam: Proposed mitigations: 1) temporarily disable adaptive-prefix-batching for orchard pool, 2) increase kvcache size/shard temporarily, 3) route traffic to orchard-prod-b3 if needed. Who can flip the config?

dmitri: I can flip the config on the orchestration layer for that pool. Will prepare a safe rollback command.

megan (support): I'll tell the customer we're investigating and will try a fallback in ~15m. They asked to be notified before routing changes.

alex: I'll stand by to open the routing rule and monitor error budget. If config rollback doesn't fix within 10m we'll fail traffic to b3 and enable lower-RT variant.

jamie: Thanks team. Action items: sam collects traces + posts flamegraph, lucas checks memory allocator/prof, dmitri prepares config rollback, alex ready to route, megan to update customer. Ping here when done.

sam: flamegraph attached (link): https://internal-artifacts/flamegraphs/1768456789-spike.svg — shows lots of time in batch key computation path and cache lookup misses.

lucas: Profiler shows jemalloc stats spike during the window. I'll correlate with eviction logs.

dmitri: rolled back adaptive-prefix-batching for orchard-prod-b4 at 19:46 UTC (config-change-id cfg-553). Watching metrics.

sam: p95 back down to ~480ms within 4m of rollback, kvcache hit rate recovered to ~90%. p99 trending down.

megan (support): relaying to customer — they confirm latency returned to normal. Customer wants RCA and mitigation plan.

jamie: Great work. After we close the ticket let's draft an RCA: include adaptive-batching change, kvcache eviction behavior, and a mitigation (canary config gating + preflight kvcache simulation). I'll take that.

alex: Can we add an automated kvcache health monitor that alerts when hitrate drops >15% in 5m? I'll add an alert proposal.

sam: Filing follow-ups: ORCH-1423 (incident notes), RTE-781 (kvcache monitor), RTE-782 (canary gating for batching).

megan (support): marking ticket as customer-notified. :white_check_mark:

jamie: closing coordination here unless anything else. Thanks everyone.
